The '''Treaty of the Concord of Istragarde''', commonly called the '''Istragarde Treaty''', was the weak postwar legal framework created after the [[Treaty Accord of 1951]]. It attempted to stabilize the world after the [[Avant Great War]] and [[Continuation War]] without creating a strong supranational government.

== Main Provisions ==

The treaty recognized sovereign borders established through the postwar settlement and required disputes to be submitted to the [[Istragarde Tribunal]]. It also defined maritime claims, discouraged unauthorized war, encouraged restraint around restricted weapons, and called for investigations into major humanitarian violations.

The treaty's language was broad and often aspirational. It created procedures and norms but did not give the Tribunal direct enforcement power.

== Enforcement ==

The Istragarde system relied on voluntary compliance, diplomatic pressure, formal condemnation, and willing coalitions. This made it useful as a common legal reference but weak against powerful or determined states.

== Historical Limits ==

The treaty became known as a stabilizing document with serious flaws. Later crises exposed its limits, including the 1971 [[Invasion of Batravalka]], the [[Volgastani Expansionist Doctrine]] in the 1980s-1990s, and maritime disputes involving [[People's Republic of Mariposa|Mariposa]], [[Imperial Rhovland|Rhovland]], and [[Astoria]].

== Territorial Expansion Failures ==

The [[Invasion of Batravalka]] became an early example of states using Istragarde language for territorial claims while avoiding meaningful enforcement. [[Karlist Perzam]] framed the 1971 invasion around historical claims and protection of Perzamic communities, but condemnation did not produce a military response.

Volgastan later followed a similar pattern. The [[Volgastani Expansionist Doctrine]] used territorial-integrity and cultural-protection language during the 1980s and early 1990s, while the [[Istragarde Tribunal]] issued rulings that it could not enforce.

== Mariposian Maritime Disputes ==

The treaty's maritime rules became especially unstable around the [[Straits of Avangard]]. The [[Mariposa-Rhovland maritime dispute]] escalated in 1983 over survey ships, oil exploration, and overlapping EEZ claims. The [[Mariposa-Astoria maritime dispute]] escalated in 1990 after a fishing-trawler seizure and an Astorian blockade.

Both disputes showed the same structural weakness: the [[Istragarde Tribunal]] could issue rulings, but it could not force states to obey them.

== Legacy ==

The Istragarde Treaty shaped postwar law but failed to prevent opportunistic expansion and ignored rulings. AGGPI later presented itself as a more active peace framework in response to the weakness of Istragarde-era enforcement.
